layout_dets.text: OCTA IMAGE SEGMENTATION TASKS

layout_dets.text: Chengliang Wang, Xinrun Chen, Haojian Ning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the analysis of optical coherence tomography angiogra-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phy (OCTA) images, the operation of segmenting specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: targets is necessary. Existing methods typically train on su-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pervised datasets with limited samples (approximately a few

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hundred), which can lead to overfitting. To address this,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the low-rank adaptation technique is adopted for foundation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model fine-tuning and proposed corresponding prompt point

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generation strategies to process various segmentation tasks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on OCTA datasets. This method is named SAM-OCTA and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: has been experimented on the publicly available OCTA-500

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset. While achieving state-of-the-art performance met-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rics, this method accomplishes local vessel segmentation as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well as effective artery-vein segmentation, which was not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: well-solved in previous works. The code is available at:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: https://github.com/ShellRedia/SAM-OCTA.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Index Terms— OCTA, Image Segmentation, Fine-tuning,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Prompt Generation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) is an in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: novative and non-invasive imaging technique that enables the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: visualization of retinal microvasculature with high resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and without needing dye injection [1]. It is a valuable tool

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for disease staging and preclinical diagnosis [2], benefits for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: monitoring lesions such as diabetic retinopathy, macular de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generation, glaucoma, and retinal vein occlusion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Xiang'an Hospital of Xiamen University

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Department of Ophthalmology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Xiamen, China

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Certain specific retinal structures, such as retinal vessels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (RV) and the foveal avascular zone (FAZ) of the macula, usu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ally need to be segmented from the raw data of OCTA for fur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ther analysis [2, 3]. Researchers have been actively exploring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deep learning-based methods for image quality assessment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and segmentation to address these challenges and enhance the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy and efficiency of OCTA image analysis. Most deep

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning segmentation methods related to OCTA are based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on self-designed neural networks and modules. This requires

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training the model from scratch, which can lead to overfitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: issues. The foundational models, trained on large-scale data,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be applied to various scenarios [4].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Shiying Li

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Segment Anything Model (SAM) was introduced as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foundational model for addressing natural image tasks. This

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: benchmark model demonstrated, for the first time, the promis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing wide applicability to various image segmentation tasks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without the need for prior re-training [5]. However, medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images differ significantly from natural images in terms of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quality, noise, resolution, and other factors, which can affect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM's segmentation performance. Thus, further research

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and optimization efforts are required to harness the potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of SAM in medical image segmentation fully [6].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We find that adopting a fine-tuning approach to SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and introducing prompt information can enhance and guide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the model's segmentation, aiming to improve some complex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA segmentation cases. We call our method SAM-OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and summarize the contributions as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) Applying Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) technology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for fine-tuning the SAM model enables it to perform effective

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation of specific targets within OCTA images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (2) A strategy for generating prompt points is proposed,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which optimizes the segmentation performance of FAZ and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: artery-vein(AV) tasks within OCTA samples.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. RELATED WORK

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1. OCTA Segmentation Models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As a typical architecture for deep image processing, the vision

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transformer (ViT) is frequently used for segmentation tasks in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA [7]. In OCTA images, the distribution of RV is exten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sive, and it requires the models to utilize the global informa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion effectively in the images. The TCU-Net, OCT2Former,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and StruNet methods have improved ViT, achieving accurate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: RV segmentation and addressing issues such as vessel discon-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tinuities or missing segments [8, 9, 10]. Other methods, from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the perspectives of efficiency, denoising, and the utilization of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three-dimensional data, have designed a series of techniques

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and strategies, achieving promising segmentation results on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA datasets [2, 11, 12, 13, 14]. The above-mentioned

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods have demonstrated that existing deep networks are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capable of achieving precise segmentation of RV and FAZ.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2. SAM and Related Fine-tuning Approaches

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The SAM is a foundational vision model for general image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation. With the ability to segment diverse objects,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parts, and visual structures in various scenarios, SAM takes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompts in the form of points, bounding boxes, or coarse

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: masks as input. Its remarkable zero-shot segmentation ca-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pabilities enable its easy transfer to numerous applications

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: through simple prompting [5]. Although SAM has estab-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lished an efficient data engine for model training, there are rel-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: atively few cases collected for medical applications or other

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rare image scenarios. Therefore, some fine-tuning methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been applied to SAM to improve its performance in cer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tain segmentation failure cases [15, 16]. The common char-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acteristic of these fine-tuning methods is that they introduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: additional network layers on top of the pre-trained SAM. With

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a small number of added trainable parameters, fine-tuning be-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comes feasible through further training on a new dataset. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: advantage of fine-tuning methods lies in their ability to pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: serve SAM's strong zero-shot capabilities and flexibility.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. METHOD

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we fine-tuned the pre-trained SAM using OCTA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: datasets and corresponding annotations. The process is shown

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Figure 1. SAM consists of three parts: an image encoder, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flexible prompt encoder, and a fast mask decoder [5].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1. Fine-tuning of Image Encoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The image encoder utilizes a ViT pre-trained with the masked

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: auto-encode method. The ViT model comes in three variants:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vit-b, vit-1, and vit-h, which can only process fixed-size inputs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., 1024 * 1024 * 3). Scaling and padding operations are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: employed to support input images of different resolutions. In

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this study, we used the image encoder from the "vit-h"model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the fine-tuning process.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As shown in Figure 2, OCTA data is inherently in 3D for-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mat, but most datasets provide en-face 2D projection forms.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: En-face projection is obtained through layer-wise segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation based on vascular anatomical structures. As SAM

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 2. OCTA structural diagram. (a) Three-dimensional vol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ume rendering with arrows indicating different projection di-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rections. (b) En-face projection. (c) B-scan projection.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires three-channel images as input, in this work, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stack projection layers of OCTA images in different depths

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to adapt to this input format. The benefit of this approach

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is that it preserves the vascular structure information in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA images while fully utilizing SAM's feature-extracting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capabilities. Fine-tuning aims to retain SAM's powerful

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image-understanding capabilities while enhancing its perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance on OCTA. The approach used in this paper involves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: utilizing the LoRA technique [17], which introduces addi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional linear network layers in each transformer block of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image encoder, similar in form to a ResNet block. During the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training process, the weights of the SAM are frozen, and only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the newly introduced parameters are updated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2. Prompt Points Generation Strategy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The prompt encoder is divided into two types of prompts:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sparse prompts (points, boxes, text) and dense prompts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (masks). In our work, we chose points as the prompt for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA segmentation. For each sample's prompt points in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: put, assuming there are n points in the prompt point input, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be represented as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where x and y denote the coordinates of prompt points in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image. The values "1" and "0" indicate positive (foreground)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and negative (background) points, respectively. The prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encoder of SAM will perform embedding on this input, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: due to its pre-training, it can appropriately integrate with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information from the input image.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The prompt points generation strategy has two types:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: global and local modes. The global mode is applied to all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OCTA segmentation tasks, while the local mode is specific to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: AV segmentation. The study of segmenting individual vessels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as a local segmentation task has not been attempted in pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vious works. By the prompt encoder, more accurate regional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessel segmentation can be achieved in OCTA datasets. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this task, the first step is to identify and label all connected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: components in the segmentation masks with unique identi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fiers. Due to the weak connectivity at the endpoints of some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels in OCTA labels, we adopt the eight-connectivity crite-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rion. Then, positive points are randomly selected within each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connected component. Due to varying numbers of vessels in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.3. Mask Decoder

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The role of the mask decoder is to efficiently map the im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: age embeddings, prompt embeddings, and output tokens to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation mask. A modified version of the transformer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder block is employed, followed by a dynamic mask pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diction head. For an image input and corresponding prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input, the mask decoder outputs multiple segmentation masks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to represent objects at different semantic levels. In this work,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the loss function (in the fine-tuning process) is computed with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the highest confidence based on the segmentation output.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. EXPERIMENTS

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1. Dataset and Preprocessing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The publicly available dataset used in this paper is OCTA-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 500 [18]. The OCTA-500 dataset contains 500 samples, clas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sified based on the field of view (FoV): 3mm * 3mm (3M)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 6mm * 6mm (6M). The corresponding image resolutions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are 304*304 and 400 *400, with 200 and 300 samples respec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tively. The OCTA-500 dataset annotates RV, FAZ, capillary,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: artery, and vein. The adopted data augmentation tool is Al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bumentations [19]. The data augmentation strategies include

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: horizontal flipping, brightness and contrast adjustment, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: random slight rotation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.2. Experimental Settings

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The OCTA-SAM is deployed on A100 graphic cards with 80

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: GB memory. To evaluate the training results, 10-fold cross-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: validation is adopted. The optimizer used is AdamW, and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning rate adopts a warm-up strategy, starting from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and gradually increasing to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The loss functions used for fine-tuning vary depending on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the segmentation tasks. For FAZ and capillary, the Dice loss is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: employed. However, for RV, artery, and vein, the clDice loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is utilized, which is more feasible for tubular segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [20]. These two loss functions can be represented as:

layout_dets.text: 4.3. Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We conducted extensive experiments with various cases on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the OCTA-500 dataset. The segmentation results using met-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rics Dice and Jaccard, which are calculated as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3.1. Global Mode

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We have experimented with various prompt point generation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strategies, including the number of points and the generation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: area for negative points. The best metrics have been selected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as the final results. RV and FAZ are common segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks in previous studies. Therefore, we will summarize the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comparative results in Table 1. The experimental data from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: previous methods are referenced from [21]. Our method's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comprehensive performance reaches the state-of-the-art level.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The impact of prompt points is insignificant for segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation tasks involving global vessels such as RV and capillary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, for FAZ, artery, and vein segmentation, prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points lead to a noticeable improvement in segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance. The segmentation results can be observed in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figures 4, 5, and Table 2. It can be inferred that the effect of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prompt point information is more pronounced within a local

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: region. For the widely distributed vessels, importing more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points can help improve the boundary delineation of the FAZ.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3.2. Local Mode

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The local mode primarily focuses on precisely segmenting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels in local regions. The segmentation targets include the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: artery and vein. For each sample, two positive points are se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lected on the target vessels and two negative points on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adjacent region.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Due to the morphological similarities between retinal ar-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teries and veins and the complexities introduced by factors

layout_dets.text: 5. CONCLUSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We propose a fine-tuning method for SAM for OCTA image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation and design prompt point generation strategies as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: global and local modes. It excels in both RV and FAZ tasks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while also firstly exploring and achieving good results in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: AV segmentation task on the OCTA-500 dataset. This is ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pected to assist in analyzing and diagnosing related diseases
